chapter: Arthur Gibbs, Savoy Ballroom and recording sessions
title: How studio sessions were run and the morning call
summary: Sessions were made up unwritten with several takes; musicians went to the Rhythm Club until the morning call.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah, nice dance record -- that was just hatched up. Well, lots of time we'd go down to the studio Stewart's -- we had a session -- they had nothing written down. We'd just -- well, this one will be so and so and so and so, and you run it down. Then the engineer was there, would take a run of it, and we'd pick out the little flaws. A lot of times we'd make a couple of masters, and when you think there they you would be the hit, the one you wouldn't pick.
Now, that's right --
(Simultaneous remarks)
That's still happening today.
(Laughter)
That's right. But (unintelligible) -- most of the recording what we did was early in the morning.
When was that?

I don't know. I guess -- well, I imagine at the time most of the musicians in Long Island -- (unintelligible) was working in the nightclub and long hours, so it would -- they catch the fellows fresh and a little (unintelligible), soon as they come out (unintelligible) ready, and they would go on down there.
Wasn't it also possible that you'd be very tired or drunk?
No, well, if they called, tell the guys like a day, couple days before, we're going down Monday morning, got a recording session (unintelligible) RCA Victor or Decca or
Melotone something like Melotone, the guys would cool it, because they get drinks down there anyway.
Well, I -- yeah, I can see that in a way, but I mean if you finish (unintelligible) at work until 3:00, 4:00 in the morning, what are you going to do between 4:00 and 9:00?
You go to -- between --
Do you go home?
Yes, you could go home if you wanted to change clothes. Lots of the guys go to the club and shoot pool.
Oh, I see.
They'd relax, shoot pool, sit up there and shoot --
You mean the Rhythm Club (unintelligible).
Yeah. And they would do all that until 10:00 o'clock, come down to the studio.

Yeah, well, I mean I could see where maybe if you -- well, you can ever then (unintelligible), you know, if you've been playing from like 9:00 until 4:00 in the morning or something, you're not necessarily going to be at your best either.
No, that's true too, because --
It would take you -- as soon as you finish work, well, then the trumpet player's chops are
liable to be tired (unintelligible).
Yeah, the trumpet would be down because them fellows -- especially the brass instruments. They be to drinking, you know, chops get down anyway.
